current_date: April 2025 ('Validation Checklist 2025', file dated April 2025 per the council's planning pages)
current_evidence: The council's 'Applying for planning permission and prior approvals' and 'Non-householder and commercial planning advice' pages both link this URL as 'Validation Checklist 2025 (pdf 3.4mb)', dated April 2025, and the mirror file on downloads.eastriding.org.uk is titled 'April 2025'.

issues.detail: The List date (2025-03-01) comes from PDF metadata (Date basis: 'PDF metadata CreationDate'). The council presents the document as 'Validation Checklist 2025', dated April 2025.
issues.evidence: Applying for planning permission page: 'Validation Checklist 2025 (pdf 3.4mb)', dated April 2025.

issues.detail: Grokbot read the superseded 'Validation Checklist August 2021.pdf' alongside the 2025 list and mixed the two in the tab. As a result many items appear twice (the site plan, roof plan and groundwater/PEA references, and the biodiversity survey three times). The tab also gives conflicting versions of the Foul Drainage Assessment Form ('Appendix 4' in the 2021 list, 'Appendix E' in 2025). The contaminated land, heritage statement and retail rows are sourced only from the 2021 document.

Householder is shown as '(none)', but the council's householder guidance names checklist items that householder applications must supply in special circumstances: Item G biodiversity survey, Item H flood risk assessment, Item J heritage statement (listed buildings), and Item R tree survey (works within 15m of a tree with a diameter of 75mm or more). A completed Design Code compliance checklist is also required, and the council lists its absence as a common reason applications are invalid.
issues.evidence: Applying for planning permission page: Items G, H, J, R and 'no completed Design Code compliance checklist'.

issues.detail: The East Riding Design Code compliance checklist is not captured as a requirement with its trigger. Grokbot's 'Design Code / Masterplan / Parameter plans' row has only the fragment 'Local Plan Design Code and the Validation Checklist).' and is placed only under Full planning. The council says the checklist is required for all development except changes of use with no material change in external appearance, and prior approvals where design is not a consideration. Outline applications also need the outline compliance checklists.
issues.evidence: Non-householder and commercial planning advice page, Design Code compliance checklist section.

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are boilerplate or navigation text, not triggers. Environmental Statement quotes advice on submitting EIA chapters on CD. Fire Statement quotes the table of contents and introduction ('Fire Statement Form ....... 100 ... Introduction 1.1'). Flood Risk Assessment and Roof plan quote the 'Top 10 reasons for invalid applications' list ('7 Missing Flood Risk Assessment 8 Missing fee'). Block plan reads 'pay online 9 Block plan error'. Design and Access Statement reads 'location plan, Design and Access Statement if specified, and a fee.' Ecological reads 'to affect protected species, eg.' Lighting reads 'Proposals for The details should include: floodlighting, such as for'. Retail reads 'Proposals for all main town centre uses The application must be accompanied by: 28'. Tree survey is a BS5837 footnote.

The 'Self-build / custom build information' row quotes Biodiversity Gain (Irreplaceable Habitat) Regulations 2024 text and the BNG self-build exemption criteria, so it is really the Biodiversity Net Gain requirement mislabelled. No BNG row exists.
issues.evidence: Trigger excerpt: '...Schedule to the Biodiversity Gain Requirements ... (Irreplaceable Habitat) Regulations [2024] ...'.

issues.detail: 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' is placed under 'Change of use - prior approval', but the source applies the tests to 'all development other than change of use applications', except changes of use to caravan, camping, chalet or mobile/park home sites. It is not a prior approval requirement.
issues.evidence: Grokbot's own excerpt: 'for all development other than change of use applications (with the exception of ...caravan, camping or chalet site...)'.

issues.detail: Several items are process text, not requirements. In tab_items: the 35-day return rule (from the 2021 list; the council now says 28 days), 'Top 10 Reasons for Invalid Applications / 60% of applications are invalid', the Planning Portal 10mb file limit, CD submission advice, redaction of personal and financial information, and repeated guidance reference lists. In app_type_rows: 'Pre-application advice' under s73 is guidance on whether changes are material amendments, and 'Planning Obligations' quotes 'it is good practice to submit... a unilateral undertaking', which is advice rather than a validation trigger.
issues.evidence: tab_items 'Submission rules'; council page: 'you are told in writing what to provide and have 28 days to respond'.

issues.detail: Almost every requirement is tagged 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', even though the checklist has Part Three type-specific checklists (only the Rural Workers Dwelling and LBC heritage checklists were used). Outline is shown as '(none)', despite the council saying outline applications need Design Code compliance checklists.
issues.evidence: Non-householder page: 'For outline applications ... the outline compliance checklists recommend which codes apply'.

summary: Grokbot's link is the current East Riding 'Validation Checklist 2025' (April 2025), but the date was taken from PDF metadata (March 2025). The PDF itself could not be read because the site blocks fetching (robots_disallowed), so missing items were checked only against the council's web pages. Those pages and Grokbot's own text show that Householder was wrongly marked '(none)', the superseded August 2021 list was mixed in, and many triggers are boilerplate or table-of-contents text.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
